corrections: Installed the complete Persian study and full corresponding English translation: 377 blocks per language, twelve sections, thirty-three subheadings, eight Quranic/lexical cards, and twenty-two Arabic quotation blocks. Used the supplied concise definition in block 374 as the registry summary. Included English transliterations and corresponding translations for every Arabic quotation, adding the immediate missing translation after the quotation in block 188.

Preserved all supplied Arabic quotations apart from formatting. Refined block 105 to describe Ibn Hayyus as a fifth-century AH poet, consistently with block 111. Refined the poem translation in block 108 to retain the temporal expression since coming to your abode. Corrected block 119 from Ibn Durayd: the sword name is Dhu al-Nun, and Dhu al-Nunayn is the dual form used for poetic requirements. Preserved the transmitted Arabic verse and the distinction between proper-name evidence, semantic evidence and historical claims.

Expanded all cited verse ranges into individual surah-and-verse references in both languages, including Ahqaf 46:5 and 46:6, Yunus 10:28 and 10:29, Saba 34:40 and 34:41, Baqarah 2:166 and 2:167, and Maryam 19:81 and 19:82. Linked only installed verified anchors. All other supplied Persian content retained.

Confirmed the single Qur’anic occurrence, nominal diddan at Maryam 19:82:6. Kept opposition distinct from mere difference, personal hatred, victory and legal contention; kept the independent filling branch separate from opposition. Preserved the argument from lahum izzan in the preceding verse to alayhim diddan, and the singular form with collective reference.

Checked Maqayis on the two independent branches; Lisan, Muhkam, Sihah and Taj on an opponent, equal, rival, filling, anger, prevailing and gentle dissuasion; Ibn Durayd on the sword name and poetic dualization; and Raghb on contraries within one genus. Checked Tabari on disavowing worship, helpers against rather than for the worshippers, enemies, companions and affliction. Retained the difference between a lexical meaning and a contextual or exegetical consequence.

All four paired lexical root assignments match QAC ROOT tags; no reassignment was needed. Updated the two own brief summaries and removed only their preliminary notices, retaining the correct existing study links and the English root label DAD D D.
